figures.alt: Aligned pressure-treated deck stair stringers on a concrete landing
figures.caption: Measure the rise, run, landing, and upper attachment before removing a stringer. Small layout changes can make every tread feel uneven.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Deck framing connection with bolted ledger, flashing, and joist hangers
figures.caption: A stair replacement ties back into the deck framing. The upper connection needs to stay sound and aligned instead of relying on a new stringer to hide movement.

figures.alt: Rock-lined drainage swale carrying roof runoff away from a Florida home
figures.caption: A firm, drained base helps outdoor wood last longer. Recheck the landing and lower stringer area after wet weather rather than allowing water to sit at end grain.
